subject: ventures/amazon-seller-profit-analyzer
professional: an Amazon FBA seller's bookkeeper / accountant (someone who reconciles the Seller Central Transaction report to the payout and to the books). First checks: does 'paid out' foot to the file's total column, are tax and fee columns handled, are refunds and partial refunds netted correctly, and is cost of goods applied to the right units.

evidence.correctness: I recomputed five outputs with code or arithmetic the author did not write. (1) Built-in sample (sampleCsv + sampleCosts): I wrote an independent Python script (scratchpad indep.py, csv.DictReader, plain sums) over the exported sample. It gives net proceeds 4515.16, operating 3075.60, profit 1310.85, and per-SKU profit PHONE-STAND-ALU 837.76, KITCHEN-SCALE-BLK 887.22, YOGA-MAT-6MM 500.73, LED-DESK-LAMP 524.70. calc.mjs analyze() gives the same figures to the cent, and so does the page loaded in Chromium ($3,076 paid out, $1,311 profit, 17.5%). Caveat: both read the file's own total column, so this checks aggregation, not Amazon's fee logic. (2) A 5-row CSV I wrote by hand in the current Seller Central column layout (sales tax, marketplace-withheld tax, regulatory fee, partial refund in the next month, a Service Fee ad row, an Order_Retrocharge row). Hand arithmetic: SKU A proceeds 27.40-15.36 = 12.04, SKU B 16.71, operating 12.04+16.71-50-1 = -22.25, profit with costs A=5, B=8 is -22.25-13 = -35.25, SKU A profit 7.04, SKU B 8.71. The tool gave -22.25, -35.25, 7.04, 8.71, and months 2026-10 / 2026-11 net -6.89 / -15.36, which I also got by hand. (3) Waterfall footing on that file: the page's waterfall lines (sales, promo, referral, FBA, other fees, refunds, refunds returned, ads, subscription, storage, reimbursements, other) sum to -22.21 but the 'Paid out' line says -22.25. The $0.04 Regulatory Fee column is in the total but not in any waterfall line, so the displayed waterfall does not foot (WRONG, small here, and it grows with that fee). (4) Partial refund: order O1 paid referral fee -6.60 on 2 units, the refund of 1 unit gave back 2.64. The tool reports 'Amazon kept $4 of referral fees' (3.96). But half the referral fee (3.30) belongs to the unit that was never refunded, so the true amount kept is 6.60/2 - 2.64 = 0.66 (which equals 20% of 3.30, Amazon's published refund administration fee rule as I remember it; I could not fetch Amazon's page to confirm). The tool overstates by 6x on any multi-unit partial refund (WRONG). (5) A refund row with a blank quantity: unitsRefunded stays 0, refund rate 0%, and full cost of goods is still charged (cogs 5, profit -9.60 on a fully refunded $20 sale) with no warning. Fee schedule: the tool contains no Amazon fee table, it reads the fees Amazon actually charged, so there is no fee-year to go stale. The sample's invented fees (e.g. $3.22 FBA on the scale, 15% referral) I did not check against the current FBA rate card; the proxy blocks Amazon pages. Score 2 because two user-facing numbers (refund-admin finding, waterfall footing) are wrong in realistic files, though the core per-SKU profit is right.
evidence.completeness: Claims checked against README and page, run in Chromium at 375px (playwright, local static server): column recognition and preamble skipping (works, calc.test.mjs and my real-layout file parsed with 0 skipped rows); per-SKU table with units, refund rate, sales, fees, paid, profit, margin (works, 4 SKUs match); waterfall (works, but does not foot with a Regulatory Fee, see correctness); monthly table (works, matches hand figures); findings: ad share, loss-makers, thin margin, refund-heavy, refund fees kept, reimbursements, storage share, fee drift, concentration (each exists in calc.mjs:290-360; ad share, refund-heavy, refund-kept and reimbursement fired on the sample, the others are covered by code paths I read but did not trigger); editable unit costs and SKU,cost paste (works, parseCosts test); 'Load an example' (works, records example_loaded); CSV download of the SKU table: the button exists and the export code (index.html:216) reads right, I did not click the download. No console errors, no off-origin requests, no horizontal scroll at 375px. No TODOs or stubs. Gaps against the stated purpose: rows not tied to a sale such as Order_Retrocharge and Refund_Retrocharge with a SKU fall into the account 'other' bucket instead of the SKU (calc.mjs:236-245), so per-SKU profit omits them; README says 'Not modelled' for these limits generally but not retrocharges.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture: 23 tests, 23 pass, about 0.3 s. Bare `node --test` (as the README says) also passes 23. The suite covers parsing, reconciliation of per-SKU proceeds to the file's totals, waterfall identity on the sample, bucketing of account rows, cost handling, refund-admin on one 1-unit case, finding triggers, page text. Seeded mutation: calc.mjs analyze(), `const costedUnits = returnsResellable ? Math.max(0, netUnits) : s.unitsSold` changed to drop the Math.max (so a SKU with more refunded units than sold units in the period gets negative cost of goods, i.e. profit inflated). Result: 23 pass, 0 fail, the mutation SURVIVED. Reverted with git checkout -- calc.mjs; `git status --short ventures/amazon-seller-profit-analyzer` prints nothing and the suite is 23/23 again. Further gaps I found by running my own cases, none covered by a test: partial multi-unit refunds (refund-admin overstated), tax and regulatory-fee columns (waterfall footing), blank refund quantity, refund in a later month than the order, retrocharge rows, FBM fulfillment counting. The sample data has only 1-unit orders and zero tax columns, so the tests cannot see these classes of bug.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (431 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Clean pure-function module, a hand-rolled CSV parser that handles quotes, BOM, CRLF and embedded newlines (calc.mjs:25-47), alias-based column finding, line-numbered skipped rows rather than silent drops, costs of missing SKUs left null not zero. Defects: (a) calc.mjs:190-196 refund-admin logic compares whole-order referral to refund referral with no quantity proration. (b) The waterfall in index.html:156-163 lists fixed lines and ignores columns that feed 'total' (Regulatory Fee, tax columns), so it does not foot. (c) calc.mjs:226 parseInt(quantity)||0 turns a blank or unreadable refund quantity into 0 silently. (d) classifyAccountRow uses description regexes like /lost|damaged|found/ that can misfile a fee with those words, but any misfiled row stays in the total. (e) sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs ('./index.html', './sitemap.xml'), which crawlers do not accept. (f) Grammar: 'on 1 refunded orders'. usage.mjs handles blocked storage and DNT/GPC well.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing is uploaded' backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR) and by my Chromium run: zero off-origin requests. Disclaimer present (index.html:125 'not legal, tax, or financial advice', no warranty, 'responsible for reviewing and verifying') and a not-affiliated-with-Amazon clause (page.test.mjs). Usage tracking: usage.mjs, csv_analyzed / example_loaded counted in localStorage only (example_loaded recorded in my run), opt-out and DNT honoured, stated on the page. README 'node --test' works. README 'reconciles to the report' holds for per-SKU proceeds (my hand file) but the waterfall shown beside it does not foot when a Regulatory Fee column is nonzero. The page text that Amazon 'gives back the referral fee less an administration fee' is fine, but the tool's dollar figure for it is wrong on partial refunds. Stale or unbacked: llms.txt points at https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/amazon-seller-profit-analyzer/, the retired redirect address (README uses https://marisstella.app/amazon-seller-profit-analyzer/). The README line 'which used to mean paying a seller-tools vendor' is marketing about competitors, not backed by a file (VENTURE.yaml names Sellerboard and others as a screening note, not a measured claim). No fake reviews.
evidence.fitness: The seller's job: from last month's Transaction CSV, find which SKUs lose money and what Amazon took. Walked through: load file, enter costs, read waterfall and findings, export CSV. For a single-month, single-marketplace, 1-unit-order FBA seller with no tax columns it works fast and the per-SKU profit is right. Hits in the first hour for a real seller: multi-unit orders with a partial refund give a wrong 'kept' number; a Regulatory Fee makes the waterfall not foot; Order_Retrocharge and other SKU-level adjustments are not charged to the SKU; a refund with blank quantity charges full COGS; no landed cost or inbound freight (disclosed as not modelled); costs must be retyped each session (no persistence); cannot compare two exports. The pre-sale fee estimation job is a different product (amazon-fba-calculator).
evidence.domain: An FBA accountant works from the same report. What they would accept: transfers excluded as payouts, ads and subscription as operating cost, reimbursements as income, COGS only on units sold net of resellable returns, missing cost left blank not zero, results labelled estimates. Where it departs from practice: (1) the output does not tie out to the payout when tax or regulatory-fee columns are nonzero; accountants reconcile to the penny first. (2) Posted-date month bucketing means a refund posted in November is charged to November while the order was October, which is correct for cash but is not shown as a limit. (3) Refund-admin handling ignores quantity, so the key refund-cost insight is unreliable for multi-unit orders. (4) No settlement-report or Business Reports (order-date basis) support, only the Transaction view. (5) No separation of marketplace-facilitator tax from seller-remitted tax. Standard compared against: Amazon's published refund administration fee (20% of the referral fee, capped at $5) from memory, not fetched; my own hand reconciliation. Not scored at 3 because tie-out fails on a realistic column set.

defects.what: Refund-admin 'referral fees Amazon kept' ignores quantity: on a partial refund of a multi-unit order it counts the referral fee of the unrefunded units as kept. Reproduced: order of 2 units, referral -6.60, refund of 1 unit returns +2.64; tool says $3.96 kept, correct admin fee is $0.66. The finding then tells the seller Amazon kept $4 on 1 order.

The waterfall omits the Regulatory Fee and any tax columns that feed 'total', so its lines do not sum to the 'Paid out by Amazon' line (-22.21 vs -22.25 in my 5-row file). A bookkeeper tying to the payout sees an unexplained gap.
defects.where: ventures/amazon-seller-profit-analyzer/index.html:156-163 and calc.mjs:171-175 (ALIASES has no regulatory fee column)

defects.what: A seeded mutation removing Math.max(0, netUnits) in the COGS line survived all 23 tests; the sample data has only 1-unit orders, no tax columns, no cross-month refunds, so whole classes of bug are invisible to the suite.
Refund row with a blank or unreadable quantity counts 0 refunded units, so refund rate is 0% and full COGS is charged with no warning (fully refunded $20 sale shows profit -9.60).
SKU-bearing adjustment rows (Order_Retrocharge, Refund_Retrocharge) go to the account 'other' bucket, not to the SKU, so per-SKU profit omits them without saying so.

llms.txt links the tool at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address; sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs ('./index.html', './sitemap.xml') which search engines do not accept; the finding text says '1 refunded orders'.

verdict: The core is sound: per-SKU proceeds, operating total, cost of goods and profit match an independent Python sum on the sample and my hand arithmetic on a 5-row file in the current Amazon column layout, to the cent, and the page loaded in Chromium shows the same numbers with no console errors, no off-origin requests and a clear disclaimer. The suite is 23/23 but a seeded COGS bug survived, and my own realistic cases found three user-visible faults: the 'referral fees Amazon kept' figure is overstated about 6x on a partial refund of a multi-unit order, the waterfall does not foot to the payout when a Regulatory Fee is present, and a blank refund quantity silently charges full cost of goods. The tool embeds no Amazon fee table, so there is no fee-year staleness to score, and I could not check the sample's invented fee levels or Amazon's refund-fee rule against Amazon's pages from this session. A bookkeeper would trust the SKU profit but not the refund-fee finding or the waterfall tie-out. Scores: correctness 2, verification 2, claims 2 (stale llms.txt, wrong refund figure), fitness 2, domain 2, completeness 3, craft 3; it does not meet the bar and is finished against its own README.
